column1: # Hand-curated motif table for the KRAS bundle.
# KRAS is not a kinase, so KLIFS does not apply and there is no pocket numbering to inherit:
# every motif here is assigned by hand, and BUILD_SPEC 5.6 requires exactly that. The app's
# ruler degrades to a plain sequence ruler for this paper.
# Regions follow the standard KRAS definitions: P-loop 10-17, switch I 30-40, switch II 60-76.
# The residues the paper actually discusses are Asp12 (the mutation), Tyr96 and Gly10.
# Applied to both deposited structures, which are the same protein and chain.

column4: Gly10. Reached by the azabicyclohexane amine through a bridging water, 2.9 and 3.1 A
Asp12. The mutation that defines the target. Compound 5a hydrogen bonds its BACKBONE N-H, never its side chain, and still holds 55-fold selectivity over wild-type KRAS
Gly13, another common KRAS mutation site
Thr35, switch I, the residue whose nucleotide contact defines the active state
Switch II begins. The loop the campaign hoped to open into an extended pocket, and which stayed shut
Gln61, the third common KRAS mutation site
His95, lines the switch II pocket
Tyr96. Direct hydrogen bond to the protonated bicyclic amine at 2.8 A: the contact that makes the rigid cage worth its synthetic trouble
Gln99, lines the switch II pocket
